words.technical: The trend composite is barely positive at about 0.09, and it averages horizons that disagree: the twelve-month and three-month readings are firmly positive while the one-month and six-month readings are negative. Range position of 0.25 is the lowest of the seven instruments, leaving spot in the bottom quarter of its own twelve-month range after a weekly fall of close to four percent. Daily volatility near 2.36% is the second highest in the set and is what stretches the one-week band from roughly 60.2 to 69.3. The stance is Flat, flipping to Hold above about 70.44 — outside the one-week band, so on these numbers a change of stance would take more than an ordinary week, and the confidence figure reflects the pooled hit rate of Flat, by some distance the best-evidenced stance in the backtest.
words.macro: Silver closed the week lower, with higher government bond yields and a firm dollar doing most of the damage before a modest Friday rebound. The bulk of the decline arrived in a single session, the metal sliding 4.6% on Wednesday before buyers returned. On Friday it outpaced gold, a pattern consistent with its double life as both a monetary and an industrial metal. Futures were quoted near 65.22 an ounce early on Friday, up 1.90%.
words.long_term: Silver's structural position rests on industrial demand from electrification and solar deployment meeting a supply base that is largely a by-product of other mining and therefore slow to respond to price. The standing consequence is a market that tends to be chronically tight and violently cyclical at once, since the industrial half of demand weakens in a downturn exactly when the monetary half is most wanted.

eoy_scenarios.central: The central band assumes the two-sided pull continues: monetary demand tracking gold under a higher-for-longer rate path, industrial demand steady, and neither strong enough to break the range before year-end.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The upside case is a precious-metals recovery in which silver's higher beta does what it usually does, amplified by any visible physical tightness in industrial supply chains.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The downside case combines a disinflation that strips out the monetary premium with a manufacturing slowdown that removes the industrial bid at the same time — the scenario in which silver's two demand sources fail together instead of offsetting.

words.technical: Crude's trend composite of about 0.66 is the strongest outside the two equity indices, and unusually it is coherent across horizons: the one-month, three-month and twelve-month readings are all clearly positive, with only the six-month reading flat. Range position of 0.64 still sits in the upper third of the past year even after a weekly fall of nearly eight percent, which says how much ground had been gained before the retreat. Daily volatility of about 2.90% is the highest of the seven instruments and produces the widest one-week band, roughly 85.0 to 100.1. The stance is Hold, flipping to Flat near 88.61 — about four percent below the close and inside the one-week band, so the reading is not far from changing.
words.macro: Crude fell on Friday as negotiators explored a phased path out of the war that would involve Tehran reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's foreign minister said the waterway could be open within a week if its conditions were met. The physical risk has not gone away, with intensifying attacks on Saudi Arabia still capable of disrupting supply from the region's largest producer. One reading offered mid-week was that neither side now has an interest in escalating further.
words.long_term: What came out of the price this week was war premium rather than any change in the physical balance, and that is the structural point: crude sits in a market with thin spare capacity and heavy dependence on a small number of chokepoints, so its risk premium is episodic and can be added or removed within days. Against that sits the slower drift of electrification and efficiency on the demand side, which caps how durable any supply-driven advance can be. Part of the headline weekly fall is also a contract effect rather than an economic one, since the front futures month rolled during the week.

eoy_scenarios.central: The central band assumes diplomacy neither collapses nor concludes: shipping stays disrupted but no worse, damaged infrastructure keeps coming back online, and prices settle in a wide range with a thinner but persistent geopolitical premium.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The upside case is a breakdown in the negotiations or a successful strike on export infrastructure, either of which restores scarcity pricing in a market with very little slack.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The downside case is a genuine reopening of the strait alongside the lifting of the blockade, releasing constrained barrels into a market where higher policy rates are already slowing demand into year-end.

words.technical: The composite of about 0.55 is carried by the three-month reading, which at roughly 1.55 is the strongest single-horizon figure anywhere in this week's set, while the twelve-month reading remains negative — the medium-term recovery has not yet repaired the longer picture. Range position of 0.70 is just inside the upper third of the past year. Daily volatility of about 2.41% is high in absolute terms but, notably, below crude's this week. The stance is Hold, flipping to Flat near 82255, roughly two percent below the close, which is a thin buffer for an instrument that routinely moves that much in a day.
words.macro: The advance that began at the end of August carried through the week. It did so against a bond market moving hard the other way, with the benchmark ten-year yield holding around 5.20% into the weekend. Fund flows have turned with the price: money into US spot exchange-traded funds is now positive for the year after erasing a substantial deficit.
words.long_term: The standing structural question is whether the asset behaves as a scarce monetary alternative or as a high-beta risk asset, and the record shows it switching between the two depending on the liquidity regime. A tightening cycle with yields at multi-decade highs is the environment in which the risk-asset reading has usually dominated, which makes this week's resilience the interesting feature rather than the size of the gain.

eoy_scenarios.central: The central band assumes flows stay mildly positive and liquidity tightens gradually rather than abruptly, leaving a wide but unresolved range into year-end.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The upside case is continued fund inflows meeting a pause in the tightening cycle, the combination that has historically separated this asset from the rest of the risk complex.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The downside case is a tightening cycle that runs further than markets expect, or a disorderly move in long yields, either of which has previously drained flows faster than they arrived.

words.technical: This carries the strongest trend composite in the set at about 1.08, built on very strong six- and twelve-month readings, with the one-month reading the weakest of the four but still positive. Range position of 0.96 puts the index within a whisker of the top of its own twelve-month range, so the starting point is an extended one. Daily volatility of roughly 0.68% is the lowest of the seven by a wide margin, which is why the one-week band spans only about 7603 to 7896. The stance is Hold, flipping to Flat near 7431 — some four percent below the close and well outside the one-week band, so the reading has room before it changes.
words.macro: The index finished the week higher, and the gain was narrow in its sourcing: the largest technology names carried it while the rest of the market did little. That happened while long-dated government yields set multi-decade records mid-week, the ten-year reaching 5.225% and the thirty-year 5.502%. One argument put to reporters was that the economy's AI-driven strength is itself the reason yields are rising.
words.long_term: The index's medium-term strength continues to rest on earnings concentrated in a small number of very large companies, which makes the aggregate more robust than the average constituent but also more exposed to any repricing of that narrow group. The standing question is whether a higher resting level of policy rates permanently lowers the multiple the market will pay.

eoy_scenarios.central: The central band assumes earnings hold up well enough to absorb a higher discount rate, leaving the index grinding within a narrow range into year-end rather than making a decisive move either way.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The upside case is inflation cooling enough to stop the tightening cycle while growth stays intact, releasing the valuation pressure that high yields are currently applying.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The downside case is yields continuing to climb from multi-decade highs and forcing multiple compression, against which a range position near the very top of the past year leaves little cushion.

The stance is Hold, flipping to Flat near 28932, about five and a half percent below the close — the widest buffer of any instrument on the page.
words.macro: The largest technology names led the week after lagging for much of the year. The case made for that leadership is that the biggest AI spenders are largely indifferent to the level of interest rates. The backdrop is an economy whose strength is concentrated in AI rather than broad-based.
words.long_term: The structural argument remains the reinvestment of very large operating cash flows into compute capacity and the returns expected from it, and the concentration that produces is both the strength and the fragility of the index. The standing risk is not that the technology story fails but that the capital intensity required to pursue it compresses the free cash flow the valuations assume.

eoy_scenarios.central: The central band assumes the current leadership holds — large technology earnings continuing to justify their premium while high yields cap further multiple expansion — leaving the index drifting near present levels into year-end.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The upside case is an earnings season that validates the capital spending, combined with any softening in the rate path that lets long-duration assets re-rate.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The downside case is a disorderly move in long yields or a disappointment from one of the handful of companies that dominate the index, either of which would meet a market positioned at the very top of its twelve-month range.

words.macro: The dollar held its gains but lost momentum into the close, finishing around 101.2. The driver was the rate outlook, with several policymakers signalling that more tightening may be coming. That repricing showed most clearly against the euro, which fell to a two-month low. The same yield surge that supported the currency took long-dated government yields to multi-decade highs during the week.
words.long_term: The dollar's standing support is the depth of its markets and its role as the default settlement and reserve currency, which makes demand for it relatively insensitive to the rate cycle. The slow structural counterweight is gradual reserve diversification, which moves on a timescale of years and has never yet been the decisive force in any single quarter.

eoy_scenarios.central: The central band assumes the rate differential behind this move persists without widening much further, leaving the index holding recent gains in a narrow range into year-end.
eoy_scenarios.upside: The upside case is the tightening that policymakers are signalling actually being delivered while other major central banks stop short, widening the gap that currency markets trade.
eoy_scenarios.downside: The downside case is inflation cooling quickly enough that the signalled path is abandoned, unwinding a move built largely on two weeks of repricing, with the fiscal concerns already cited as a brake doing the rest.

coherence.note: The dollar and crude both carry a Hold stance this week even though their documented relationship is negative, because each was moved by its own story rather than by the other: the dollar rose on a repricing of the interest-rate path, while crude's weekly fall came from war premium being taken out of the price and, in part, from the front futures contract rolling to a cheaper month — neither of which has to appear as a mirror image in the currency.

week_summary: Two forces set the week: a bond market that pushed long-dated yields to their highest in roughly two decades, and a Middle East war in which diplomacy suddenly looked possible. The first pressed on precious metals, taking silver down close to four percent and gold lower with it; the second removed nearly eight percent from US crude, though some of that move reflects the front futures contract rolling to a cheaper month rather than a fall within a single contract. Equities absorbed both and finished higher, led almost entirely by the largest technology names, while the dollar managed a second consecutive weekly gain on the rate outlook. Gold is not scored this week: a scheduled US inflation release falls inside the gate window, so the model declines a reading rather than guessing through it. Six of the seven instruments carry a stance, and the pooled record is the honest caveat — Hold has held a little under 57% of the time historically, and five of the six readings on this page are Hold, while silver's Flat is the only one resting on a strong historical base. The range model's own coverage sits near 88% against an 80% target, but on only 33 observations, which is still too short a record to lean on.
